newsitem.title: USA: EDS seeks to drum up Year 2000 business - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: EDS seeks to drum up Year 2000 business - WSJ.

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp plans to spend $144 million to update its computers to work properly in the year 2000, and hopes to bring in $1.3 billion in business helping other companies deal with the problem, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Wednesday's edition, the Journal said complications from the way computers read the 2000 number could be an especially troublesome problem for EDS, which has a large customer base and operates a variety of systems.
EDS Executive Vice President Stuart Reeves said the company hopes the new millenium-related business will generate between $200 million and $250 million in profit over three years.

The company is currently negotiating Year 2000 conversion contracts worth about $350 million, Reeves said. To help with the new business, EDS is hiring several hundred programmers and calling some out of retirement this year.
